associations.rationale: The formal type only computes the cardinality of a parameter index; it does not itself assert the source's existence, irreducibility, or distinctness claims about representations.
The character-parameter equivalence is a construction used to organize the homomorphisms in the source, rather than a displayed claim about the resulting representations.
This type constructs a family of representations from an index but does not state their irreducibility, classification, character values, or count.
The implication from isomorphism of two family members to equality of their indices directly states the source's distinctness claim up to the chosen parameter identification.
The formal type directly says every member of the complementary family is simple, matching the source's assertion that the resulting representations are irreducible.
This declaration constructs a representation from a character satisfying the non-Frobenius-fixed condition, but its type alone does not state the source's character or irreducibility conclusions.

The type gives a Frobenius isomorphism for complementarySeriesRep, whereas the displayed source isomorphism is specifically between the induced representations; this is related supporting evidence, not the same stated claim.
The type identifies the character with the opaque name complementarySeriesChar, without displaying the scalar, parabolic, hyperbolic, or elliptic formulas from the source.
The stated iff says two complementary representations are isomorphic exactly when their parameters agree or differ by Frobenius, directly matching the source's parameter identification.
The formal conclusion directly asserts simplicity of the complementary-series representation under the displayed non-Frobenius-fixed hypothesis, matching irreducibility in the source.

This type directly packages a family of simple pairwise nonisomorphic representations whose index has cardinality q(q-1)/2, which is the source's representation-family and count claim rather than a bare cardinality consequence.
The finrank equality q - 1 is obtained by specializing the source's scalar character formula at the identity, so it is a supporting consequence rather than the claim exactly stated in the passage.
